facts.text: On this date in 1513, Vasco Núñez de Balboa became the first European to see the Pacific Ocean — after crossing Panama on foot with 190 men and a pack of war dogs.
On this date in 1962, Algeria held its first post-independence elections. The country had lost roughly 1.5 million people in eight years of war against France.
Manila is the most densely populated city on Earth — over 111,000 people per square kilometer, denser than any neighborhood in New York or Tokyo.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than inside one drawn around London — despite the London circle being three times larger.
Canada has more lakes than every other country combined, holding roughly 60% of the world's fresh lake water, yet ranks among the worst per capita for water security planning.

On this day in 1555, the Peace of Augsburg was signed — but the real settlement was financial: it made sovereign debt a European norm, as princes needed bond markets to fund newly independent churches and armies.

On September 25, 1690, the first American newspaper, Publick Occurrences, was shut down after one issue. Its publisher had planned a financial column. Boston's authorities killed both on the same day.

The S&P 500 has closed higher on the last trading day of September more often than not — but the month itself is statistically the worst calendar month for stocks, a pattern that has held across 12 decades.

Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway began as a failing textile mill. The original sin: Buffett bought it out of spite after a manager lowballed him by 0.125 cents per share. He later called it the worst trade of his life.
The Dutch tulip mania of 1637 peaked with a single Semper Augustus bulb fetching 10,000 guilders — roughly the price of a canal house in Amsterdam. The crash that followed took less than a week.

On this date in 1973, Skylab 3 astronauts returned to Earth after 59 days in orbit — their bones had aged faster than their clocks, a quiet proof that gravity and time are the same thing bent differently.
On September 25, 1957, the first commercial nuclear power plant came online in Pennsylvania, splitting atoms to boil water — the most expensive way humans have ever made steam.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces roughly 3.8 million cells per second. The you that existed a year ago shares almost no physical material with the you reading this now.
Octopuses have three hearts, blue blood, and neurons distributed throughout their arms — each limb thinks semi-independently, making them closer to a colony than a single creature.
On this day in 1513, Balboa became the first European to see the Pacific Ocean — standing on a peak in Panama, days before anyone in Europe learned he'd even left the Atlantic coast.
On this day in 1962, the first James Bond film began production. It was released the same year Algeria gained independence and the Cuban Missile Crisis nearly ended civilization.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. The freshman lecture halls predate Tenochtitlán by three centuries.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The pyramid is that old.
The fax machine was invented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, and 17 years before the Pony Express, which it could have made unnecessary.

Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): the wordless look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The Yaghan people of Tierra del Fuego compressed an entire social drama into one word.
Meraki (Greek): to do something with soul, pouring yourself into it so completely that a piece of you remains in the work. English has no equivalent.

On this day in 1513, Balboa became the first European to see the Pacific Ocean — and he waded into it fully armored, sword drawn, claiming the entire sea for Spain. The Spanish word for this audacity is demasía.
Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic longing for something beloved that may never return. Linguists debate whether it can truly be translated; most conclude it cannot.

On this day in 1066, William the Conqueror landed at Pevensey, beginning the conquest that would flood English with Norman French — giving us pairs like ask/question, wedding/marriage, and kingly/royal that still encode a class divide.

On this date in 2022, Ethereum completed The Merge, switching from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake. Energy consumption dropped 99.95% overnight — the largest carbon footprint reduction in computing history.
On this date in 2021, El Salvador's Bitcoin wallet Chivo crashed within hours of launch due to demand. The government quietly took it offline for two hours while holding legal tender status for BTC.

Bitcoin's first real-world transaction — 10,000 BTC for two pizzas in 2010 — used a bounty posted on BitcoinTalk. The buyer never moved the coins himself; a volunteer in the UK actually ordered the pizza.
The DAO hack of 2016 didn't steal ETH — it drained it into a child DAO with a 28-day lock. Ethereum forked before the attacker could withdraw a single coin, making the theft technically incomplete.
Satoshi Nakamoto's known wallets hold roughly 1.1 million BTC, none of which have ever moved. On-chain analysts track them by their early coinbase pattern — sequential mining across 54,000+ blocks.
On this date in 2015, Google open-sourced TensorFlow — a move that shifted deep learning infrastructure from lab curiosity to global commodity almost overnight.
On this date in 2022, DeepMind's AlphaFold database crossed 200 million predicted protein structures, covering nearly every catalogued organism on Earth.
The original transformer paper, 'Attention Is All You Need,' was submitted by eight authors — all of whom left Google within five years of publication.
Training GPT-4 is estimated to have consumed more electricity than 1,000 US households use in a year, yet its weights compress into roughly 1TB of disk space.
RLHF — the technique that makes large language models follow instructions — was first applied to summarization tasks in 2020, not to chatbots; the chatbot use came two years later.
